title: The party at Mills and the jam session
summary: Greene and the Danses recall Helen Dance's party, his first jam session, where everyone was present.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, let's go back now just one second to our party at Mills. Because Freddy and I decided, he's giving me a plug on this one.
I said, Freddy remembers that part...
Of course I remember it. I remember it was very exciting for me.

You know? And, when I walked in I saw alot of people. But then I saw her -- I saw Helen. And she was so busy, and looked so happy, and so friendly, you know what I mean, that she really made an impression on me.
That's when I really met her, too.
Yeah. Didn't you get that feeling when you first met her?
Yeah. Well, the thing that I liked was that -- all the girls that I knew, you know, used to like gin and lime -- and she liked chocolate sodas.
And I can remember she had a 'bob' hair -- you know, what do you call it? Oh, she was cute. (laugh)
But, that was a hell of a jam session, though.
Oh, it was out of sight.
Oh, listen, it was the most exciting thing, you know, to me, you know. When I walked in, you know what I mean, and everybody was there.
a little later you couldn't do it.
I know, but that session of yours really was something else.
It really was something wasn't it, because the stature...
And, that was my first session, more or less, you know.
You see, I'd never witnessed anything like that.
You see, I didn't realize. I was telling Freddie that it was a big thing for me -- are we still alright --

-- because I said that Basie and Lester were giving me a whole lot of beautiful jive about it. They were coming to me -- coming to New York you know, they had just covered Europe, and they were coming to me -- especially Basie, you know was saying -- 'I've been waiting to, you know --

He used to tell me that they used to sit up at night in the bus and talk about this -- 'who is this gal writing these things in her waiting we need to come to New York. And he was giving me all this stuff, you know, and even Lester was, you know. So, I said, this is one of my big memories that I have -- big moment for me.

You know, I got that feeling -- even though I was much younger -- I felt this -- you know, when I walked in.
